title: IPv4: classes, public and private addresses, loopback and broadcast

videos.script: Every machine in this office has an address like ten, twenty, ten, twenty-one. Four numbers and three dots. {{address}} It looks like a label somebody typed. It is a number, thirty-two bits long, and almost everything this course does with addresses is arithmetic on those bits. {{bits}} In this lesson you will read pc1's address in binary, with a calculator called ipcalc. You will meet the old classes, A, B and C. The calculator still prints them, and nobody plans a network with them any more. {{classes}} Then the ranges that carry a meaning of their own. Private addresses, which never cross the internet. The one public address the router uses for the whole office. And loopback, where a machine talks to itself. {{ranges}} Last, broadcast: one ping sent to every machine on the network at once. The first time, nobody answers. You will see why, and what it takes to get a reply. {{broadcast}} The office is the lab this course is built on: four computers, a switch and a router, all on one Linux machine. Every output on the screen is the one it really printed. {{lab}}
